title: Turning geologic raster collections into accessible GIS layers
summary: I built a Python workflow to convert more than 400 geologic rasters into polygon datasets for web GIS publication. The work connected repeatable spatial processing with the NETL interactive atlas, preparing scientific data so researchers could explore basin-specific layers through an accessible mapping interface.
role: Geospatial data scientist · Raster-to-vector automation and data preparation
context: Leidos research supporting DOE/NETL · Geologic data visualization

image.alt: Appalachian Basin interactive map showing earthquake locations, structural lineaments, and geophysical raster layers
image.caption: NETL atlas screenshot: the Appalachian Basin view combines earthquake observations, structural features and geophysical layers. The application is a collaborative product; my contribution was data-processing automation.

problem: Hundreds of geologic raster files needed to become usable web-mapping layers. Repeating conversion and preparation manually would make the collection difficult to process consistently and maintain for visualization.
contribution: I developed the Python automation that processed more than 400 raster files into vector polygon datasets and prepared the outputs for GIS publication. My contribution focused on the processing and data-delivery workflow, rather than claiming sole authorship of the NETL atlas or every layer it displays.

approach.title: Process a large raster collection repeatably
approach.body: Applied a scripted raster-to-vector workflow across the geologic file collection, replacing repeated manual conversions with a consistent processing sequence.

approach.title: Prepare the GIS outputs for delivery
approach.body: Produced vector polygon files suitable for upload and use in the web GIS environment. Data preparation connected the source rasters to layers that could be organized and explored online.

approach.title: Support basin-based visualization
approach.body: Prepared outputs for the NETL interactive atlas, where thematic controls let users inspect geologic and structural information within basin-specific maps.

outcome: The workflow prepared hundreds of geologic datasets for web-based GIS use and supported their presentation in the NETL atlas. The public application demonstrates the delivery context: users can explore basin maps, thematic layer categories and individual formation datasets. Original processing scripts are not public.
learning: The project demonstrates the step from performing a spatial operation to delivering a repeatable data service workflow. It connects batch processing, consistent spatial outputs and publishing requirements, a transferable pattern for moving research datasets into interfaces that other people can use without running the underlying code.
limitations: The original conversion scripts are not publicly available, so the case study documents the contribution and delivery context rather than a runnable implementation.
Atlas screenshots show a collaborative application and multiple data sources; they are not evidence that I authored every displayed dataset or the full application.
The work prepares and visualizes geologic information. It does not by itself certify a site’s suitability for carbon storage.

evidence.title: Scale of the processing contribution
evidence.body: The documented workflow processed more than 400 geologic rasters into vector polygon files for GIS publication. No unmeasured time-saving or business-impact estimate is attached to that count.
